title: The Rogueries of Dalilah the Crafty

keywords: the rogueries of dalilah the crafty
full_text:
In Baghdad, during the reign of Harun al-Rashid, lived an extraordinarily clever woman named Dalilah, whose sharp mind and theatrical agility were famous across the markets. Following the death of her husband, an honest city officer, the palace bureaucrats refused to grant her family their lawful pension, mocking her appeals.

Dalilah resolved to prove that her intellect was more powerful than all the ministers of state.

She embarked upon a series of harmless, dazzling pranks across the city: she persuaded an arrogant silk merchant that she was the daughter of an emir, borrowed fifty bolts of brocade, and paid him with an order on the city judge; she sold a donkey to a gullible broker twice in the same afternoon; and disguised as an imperial inspector, she entered the police headquarters, confiscated the chief’s silver seal, and left a basket of dry onions in its place!

All Baghdad was in an uproar, laughing at the mysterious 'trickster' who outwitted magistrates and merchants without shedding a single drop of blood or retaining stolen property.

When Harun al-Rashid offered an amnesty to whoever was performing these feats if they would reveal their identity, Dalilah walked boldly into the imperial audience hall, returned every bolt of silk, every coin, and the police chief’s silver seal with a polite bow!

The Caliph laughed until tears streamed down his cheeks, astonished by her incomparable wit and organizational genius.

Instead of punishing her, Harun al-Rashid granted her the full pension, appointed her Chief Superintendent of the Imperial Post and Courier System of Baghdad, decreeing that a woman who could outwit all his guards was the best person to safeguard the communications of the empire.
moral: Resourceful wit and clever audacity can outmatch the most rigid bureaucracy and win royal recognition.
